dns.about_before: A separate box, a sealed token: the broker is its own sealed service, the write token never leaves it, and minting grants runs through the domain's authority. Granting and requesting certificates run over the mesh —
dns.about_mid: — and the peer plumbing lives on
dns.budget_body: Per-domain and per-name weekly issuance ceilings with pre-flight refusal, so one flapping host can never exhaust a domain's Let's Encrypt budget. The ledger above already records what a rail would count.
dns.ddns_body: A moving node re-points its own A-record by signed update — same cert, no new issuance, no budget spent. Designed, not built.
dns.drop_cred_body: The token is encrypted at rest and never read back to any screen. Setting it makes this box able to broker the domain.
dns.how_1: A name is chosen — the grant names exactly one host under a brokered domain.
dns.how_2: The A-record is written FIRST — DNS is identity, and a cert never points at nothing.
dns.how_3: The ACME proof runs — Let's Encrypt issues against the live record.
dns.how_4: The node serves on a real certificate — renewals repeat the same path.
dns.how_title: How a name becomes a certificate
dns.intro: Real names and real certificates for mesh nodes: an authority grants, a broker writes the record and proves the name, and the node serves on a real cert. The token that writes DNS is sealed on the broker box — write-only, encrypted, never shown to anyone again.
dns.ledger_cite: Append-only — every certificate this broker ever issued.
dns.no_authz: No live broker authorizations known to this box.
dns.no_creds: No domain credentials on this box.
dns.no_creds_after: A box only needs one when it brokers a domain — most nodes never do.
dns.pername_body: One grant, one host name — the only ungated path, tried first, budget-cheap.
dns.routing_body: Signed attestations — which broker may act under which domain, per the domain's authority. Gossiped across the mesh; a mint can never outrun it.
dns.signin_body: Credentials, grants and the issuance ledger are shown only to a signed-in operator of this box.
dns.wildcard_body: A distinct grant kind touching the protected trust core: authority-minted, per-domain approval, optionally a higher consent bar. Designed, not built.

identity.att_after: . Never credentials, never locations, never ballots. Roles are still derived live, never stored.
identity.att_before: Role codes, the device key, the issuer, a TTL, and a signature — and
identity.att_cite: voting and candidacy are absolute rights, derived from residency, never persisted
identity.att_strong: An attestation carries only public standing.
identity.check_action_detail: The device signed THIS exact write (form + payload + subject) — non-repudiation.
identity.check_attestation_detail: The issuer’s pinned key verifies the snapshot — fails closed on expiry, revocation, or mutation.
identity.check_subject_detail: The attested user resolves locally before the engine authorizes.
identity.devices_caption: The enrolled operator device keys on this box
identity.devices_intro: Each device enrols its own key. Possession of a device key — never a password — is what other servers recognise.
identity.enrol_body: A device enrols its Ed25519 PUBLIC key — the secret never leaves the device (no escrow).
identity.enrol_lr_after: key is published; the secret half never leaves the device. There is nowhere for a private key to be escrowed.
identity.enrol_note: Enrolment publishes a device’s public key; linking proves possession of an already-enrolled key on a new box. No secret ever leaves the device.
identity.forwarded_intro: When a forwarded write arrives, it must clear all three checks before the engine will authorize it. Any failure is fail-closed.
identity.intro: The identity layer that lets a server know who you are across the mesh, and lets a citizen’s public standing travel with them onto a server that isn’t home. Two separate identities live here — yours as an operator, and the attested standing of a citizen passing through. They never touch.
identity.keystone_body: The forwarded write is the keystone: a person passing through a server that isn’t home can still act, because their standing travels as a signed, short-lived attestation and their own device signs the action itself.
identity.keystone_cite: standing travels; the right itself stays derived, never stored
identity.lr_password: Your local password signs you in on this box only — other boxes recognise you by device-key possession, never by a password.
identity.no_devices_body: This operator account signs in with its local password only. Enrolling a device publishes its Ed25519 public key, so other boxes can recognise you by key possession.
identity.no_mesh_id_body: This box has not cut its Ed25519 signing keypair. It mints the first time federation needs it — reading this page never mints one.
identity.not_linked: not linked to a mesh identity yet
identity.public_key_label: Public key (Ed25519 — the public half only)
identity.secret_note: The secret half of the signing key never leaves this box and never rides this page. Peers pin the public key; the node signs as itself.
identity.signin_body: The identity plane is shown only to a signed-in operator. Nothing here carries constitutional power — it is how this box proves which box is talking.
identity.subject_note: Subject: the attested user resolves locally before authorization — citizenship is read live, never trusted from the wire alone.
identity.sweep_body: A housekeeping job prunes lapsed attestations (already fail-closed on expiry; the sweep just bounds the table, soft-deleting for forensics).
identity.travel_intro_after: . This attestation is what lets a visiting player act here.
identity.travel_intro_before: A person on a journey can act through a server that isn’t their home, because their public standing travels as a signed, short-lived
identity.two_id_body: Your operator account proves which box is talking; a citizen’s attestation proves what they may do. Neither can be read as the other — and neither buys a constitutional privilege.
identity.wall_body: Operator identity is wholly separate from citizen identity — an operator account has no link to any citizen user.
identity.wall_strong: The plane wall holds here too.
identity.what_att_body: A short-lived (≤ 24h), revocable, instance-signed snapshot of a person’s derived standing, bound to a device key. Only the HOME authority attests. It carries only public standing — never credentials, locations, or ballots.
identity.what_att_cite: Only the home authority attests · ≤ 24h · revocable · instance-signed
identity.your_identity_intro: Who this box is on the mesh, and who you are on this box. This is infrastructure identity — it grants no vote, no seat, no constitutional say.

mesh.about: This console reads the mesh as it is — peers from the handshake registry, our advertised transports, the live peerage gates, and the last 25 entries of the append-only sync ledger. Every join, sync and departure it shows was recorded by the federation services; the page changes nothing. Cluster join is infrastructure, not a constitutional act: it grants no vote, no seat, and no authority over any place's record.
mesh.authority_after: node: the action is verified — signed by their own device, carrying an attestation from their home server — and forwarded to the place's home copy.
mesh.authority_before: For every jurisdiction, one box's record is the authoritative one — a bookkeeping fact about where the home copy lives, never a rank. A player can act on
mesh.becoming_before: There is one path to peerage, and every node walks it: get a certificate, take clients, and hold the whole public record. Once you're in, your box is a full, equal peer — it serves players like any other node. Role elevation is the separate, trust-gated ladder on
mesh.differ_body: Only two things. Services a box's hardware can't host — a small box might skip voice or the live rooms. And the trust-gated naming channels, which reach under other peers' zones and so need those peers' consent.
mesh.federation_url: Federation URL — how peers address this box:
mesh.ffc_body: When peers carry one another's records, the sync ledger is the receipt. Each row is one push or pull, with its result and the record range it covered. An “authority disputed → resolved” result means the dispute resolved in favour of the place's home copy — the constitutional record never forks.
mesh.ffc_title: Full Faith & Credit — the sync ledger
mesh.gates_body: What this box still needs before (or to remain) a full peer — a certificate, an identity, a reachable URL. Each gate is probed live; nothing here is a rank, only readiness.
mesh.intro: How your node finds its peers, carries their records, and survives a hostile network — the federation layer the citizen game rides on.
mesh.ledger_lr_after: — like every record on the constitutional plane, it can be read by anyone and never rewritten.
mesh.moving_body: When a home box retires (or its government chooses a new host), authority moves in three verified steps:
mesh.moving_note: Nothing is lost and nothing pauses: reads continue everywhere throughout, and forwarded writes queue until the flip lands.
mesh.no_peers_after: . Joining never moves authority: which box holds a place's home copy stays exactly where it was.
mesh.no_peers_before: No peers yet — this box stands alone. Joining a cluster starts with a one-shot join-key minted by a host operator; the join wizard is on
mesh.no_sync: No sync entries yet — the ledger starts writing the moment a peer carries records to or from this box.
mesh.no_transports: No transports advertised yet — peers can still reach this box at its federation URL below, but registering transports gives the mesh fallback rungs when that URL fails.
mesh.open_controls: Open connection, invitation, and access controls
mesh.peerage_cite: One process to peerage — authority attaches to a place, never a node
mesh.peers_body: Every box this node has handshaked with, and where each one sits in the trust lifecycle. The relation chip records how you stand to each peer — it describes data placement, never a rank.
mesh.plane_off_body: Joining, syncing and naming peers are capabilities — they buy no vote, no seat, and no say in any constitutional act.
mesh.relation_mirror: holds no place’s home copy here — still a full peer for reads and forwarded writes
mesh.relation_sovereign: a peer with its own home copies — we sync both ways
mesh.signin_body: Peers, transports and the sync ledger are shown only to a signed-in operator of this box. Citizens play the game; operators keep the box on the mesh.
mesh.step_export_body: — the departing box seals a signed export of the jurisdiction's records.
mesh.step_flip_body: — the receiving peer verifies it against the audit chain, and the mesh records the new home.
mesh.step_repeer_body: — every other node re-points at the new home copy on its next sync.
mesh.transports_before: The same signed bytes ride any advertised channel, tried in priority order — so the mesh survives even when the open internet does not. These are the endpoints
mesh.trust_lifecycle: Trust lifecycle: discovered · handshake · trust established · syncing · border settled
moderation.about_before: Preserve → report → purge is the M-5 sequence; a removal never server-ACLs a peer and never records a hash. See it from the citizen side on
moderation.above_body: Only a live, key-pinned judicial attestation (R-19/R-20) removes anything. The operator is no longer honoured — by code, not policy.
moderation.below_body_after: , so it can never be mistaken for a judge's ruling.
moderation.below_body_before: The operator may relay a rights-protection removal — logged with basis
moderation.carve_m1_who: A judge — once a government is seated
moderation.carve_m2_who: Operator relay below the flip → judicial above it
moderation.carve_m3_who: Each person, their own screen only
moderation.flip_body: The flip is automatic — a pure function of facts, never a manual mode change. Below: the operator board relays narrow protections. Above: only a live judicial attestation removes anything.
moderation.intro: The operator holds no power to remove on viewpoint — hosting buys no say. Below the flip an operator can only relay narrow protections, everything logged; the moment a government seats itself, removal authority passes to judges and the operator's relay leg closes automatically.
moderation.legal_csam_effect: Purges the bytes — delete, not quarantine
moderation.legal_floor_body: An operator account by key-possession — not a standing attestation, off the constitutional plane. The list of legal bases is closed, grown only by code release; the list SOURCE is recorded, never the hash; the trail is append-only.
moderation.legal_floor_cite: Key-possession · closed list · append-only sealed trail · F-SOC-004
moderation.no_content_control: There is no "remove for content" control.
moderation.no_content_control_after: It does not exist to be granted, delegated, or seized — a per-user block affects only the blocker's own screen and is never recorded anywhere.
moderation.signin_body: The sealed moderation trail is shown only to a signed-in operator of this box.
moderation.trail_empty_after: No carve-out has ever been invoked and no legal-floor removal has ever been filed on this box.

roles.approval_cite: Approval mints a verified grant — dual-meter consent (Art. VII admissibility; seated-government supersession), never a self-claim. Dropping one of your own channels is always unilateral.
roles.channels_caption: The nine capability channels, their consent kind, live state on this node, and actions
roles.field_scope_hint: Leave blank for the root jurisdiction. A grant acts over a place — never over the mesh as a rank.
roles.founding_body: There is no mesh to answer to and no government seated yet, so every role is yours to switch on directly — governed channels included. Once your world is founded and a government seats, governed channels return to the dual-meter consent path for any later change.
roles.four_roles_intro: Four friendly names group the nine channels — no new power, just a grouping. Each card shows its channel set, the duty you take on, and whether it turns on by itself or needs a government decision.
roles.governed_gloss: Governed — requested, then dual-meter approval (operator board, or the seated government).
roles.intro: A box’s “role” is nothing more than the set of capability channels it runs. Trust here is composable — you add the channels you can serve, one at a time. There are no tiers to climb and no rank to earn.
roles.life_approve: the dual-meter consents — operator board, or the seated government
roles.life_join: the channel turns on; it now shows as Active
roles.life_qualify: the node proves it can run the channel (reachable, on the right version, and has the storage and data the channel needs)
roles.life_request: the operator asks for the capability over a named peer or jurisdiction
roles.lifecycle_intro: A governed channel walks four plain steps. A self-asserted channel skips straight to Active — there is no request and no approval to wait on.
roles.meter_a_applies: the bootstrap path, before a government is seated
roles.meter_b_applies: the moment a legislature is seated — it SUPERSEDES Meter A
roles.meter_b_who: the constituent legislatures, by supermajority (a multi-jurisdiction vote)
roles.meter_c_applies: only channels that act under a peer’s zone — broker.dns, authority.grant
roles.meter_c_title: acts under a peer’s zone — co-affected peers must consent
roles.meter_c_who: every peer whose subtree the channel would touch
roles.never_rank: — never to a node as a rank.
roles.nine_intro_1: The whole closed vocabulary. Three channels are
roles.nine_intro_2: — and need no gate at all: they only ever describe what your own box does. The other six are
roles.nine_intro_3: , because each one grants a duty over others, or hangs a name under a peer’s zone.
roles.no_pending: No open role-grant requests. A governed request you or a peer opens will appear here with its live meter state.
roles.pending_caption: Open role-grant requests with live consent-meter reads
roles.petition_gloss: Read–write authority is a fact about a place — where its home copy lives. It moves between consenting nodes per jurisdiction; it is not a rank this box petitions for.
roles.plane_off_body: Running a node is infrastructure, not a citizen privilege — it buys you no extra vote, no seat, no say in any constitutional act. Operator accounts have no link to citizen users.
roles.probe_meter_c: This channel acts under a peer’s zone — co-affected peers must also consent (Meter C).
roles.run_step_body: Qualify probes whether this box can host the channel — it changes nothing. Request turns a self-asserted channel on, or opens a governed request for the dual-meter to decide.
roles.seated_gloss: A seated government approves through its own vote — this button can only attest Meter A, and the grant will refuse with its citation until that vote passes.
roles.self_gloss: Self-asserted — every channel goes live on one click; no gate.
roles.self_vs_gov_body: A self-asserted channel touches nobody but you, so it is yours to switch on. A governed channel either grants a duty over other people or writes a name under a peer’s zone — so it is requested, never claimed, and approved by the dual-meter below.
roles.signed_in_grant: Signed in as {name} · a grant always attaches to a place
roles.signin_body: The roles board is shown only to a signed-in operator. Operator accounts live on the operator plane — they have no link to citizen users and carry no citizen power.
roles.waiting_dual_meter: Waiting on the dual-meter — see the pending list below.
roles.waiting_intro: A governed channel is approved by a dual-meter — operators while no government is seated, the seated government the moment one exists — plus a third meter for the few channels that reach under a peer’s zone. The meters below are live reads; nothing here re-counts a vote.
sim_console.chamber_note: A chamber exists as soon as a place is activated, but only an election puts people in it — seating anyone without one would manufacture members nobody voted for. An empty chamber is the correct state, not a failure.
sim_console.draft_after: until adopted, and a chamber above nine seats cannot elect without an adopted one.
sim_console.halt_requested: Halt requested — workers stop at their next claim boundary, never mid-item. Clearing the flag resumes exactly where it stopped.
sim_console.no_run_after: — this page comes alive within the minute, when the pump seeds its first workers.

sim_console.over_bound_body_before: Art. V §3 binds the Type B chamber to the Type A total. These exceed it: the seat ladder floors at two seats per constituent and cannot go lower, and the next step — grouping constituent jurisdictions into shared panels — is not built. A chamber marked
sim_console.paused: Paused by the database breaker until {until} — a Postgres restart was detected. This pauses claims; it never abandons work.
sim_console.people_minted_note: People minted is deliberately far below population modelled: identity is materialized only where the constitution requires it — a candidate, a member — and everyone else is counted exactly as a cohort rather than stored as a row.

sim_console.seat_gap_body: The cube-root law fixes how many seats a chamber has; its districts must sum to exactly that. Where they do not, the difference is seats the constitution declares and no election can fill — every count lands short, permanently. This is a defect in the district plan, and only redrawing it repairs it.
sim_console.smoke_hint: A smoke limit enumerates only the N largest jurisdictions — leave it blank to populate the whole set. Enumeration runs on the queue; the bars come alive within the minute.
sim_console.subtitle: Live. Refreshes every 2 seconds from the work queue itself — no cached counters.
versioning.about: This console renders the versioning truth held by the upgrade-agreement service — it never re-implements a meter or moves a version itself. Proposals are driven through the mesh services; a regressive constitutional bump can never pass the hardened filter, no matter who consents.
versioning.answerable_body: Operators run the upgrade; they never author the rule. The filter is hardened, the freeze is mechanical, and the seated government has the final say.
versioning.const_version_cite: the constitutional version — a fingerprint of the hardened rules in force
versioning.derived: derived from the rules in force
versioning.failclosed_body: A divergent version stops the sync rather than silently merging mismatched rules. The other side agrees the upgrade — through the same meters below — before its tail flows again.
versioning.freeze_body: When play begins, the contest captures the constitutional version in force at that moment. Any agreed upgrade lands for the next contest — never the one mid-play — so no one can change the rules under the ballots already cast.
versioning.freeze_note: Pinning is a pure function of the contest record; there is no manual override to thaw a running game.
versioning.freeze_strong: A running election or session pins its version.
versioning.intro: How a version changes hands across the mesh — what this node runs, what every peer advertises, and the open proposals waiting on consent. Every constitutional change is screened by the hardened filter first, then agreed by the people who actually hold the power.
versioning.leg_board: the operator board (no government seated yet)
versioning.meters_cite: A and B are two legs of one seat — the operator board attests only while no government is seated; the moment one seats, its supermajority supersedes the board. C is every trust-established peer holding the home copy of a co-affected place (unanimous; it passes on its own when no such peer exists).
versioning.no_meters: no meters — this kind moves mechanically
versioning.no_peers: No peers yet — this box stands alone. Versions start to matter the moment a second box joins the mesh.
versioning.no_proposals: No open proposals — the mesh agrees on the version in force.
versioning.peer_caption: Peer constitutional versions and app releases
versioning.peer_versions_body: Every peer advertises its constitutional version. A peer on a different version cannot be synced into — the mesh refuses fail-closed until both sides have agreed an upgrade.
versioning.plane_off_body: Upgrading the software is an operator-plane capability, not a citizen privilege. The constitutional rules themselves are never edited from here — a version change is proposed, screened, and only then agreed by the people who actually hold the power.
versioning.proposals_body: A proposal is screened first, agreed second. Each meter that applies must pass; a meter that doesn't apply to the proposal's kind or scope simply isn't needed.
versioning.screened_body: Every proposal passes the hardened admissibility filter before any consent is counted. One that would lower proportionality, or drop the supermajority floor below majority-plus-one, is refused outright — no meter, no operator, and no amount of reach can wave it through.
versioning.signin_body: Versions and upgrade proposals are shown only to a signed-in operator. Nothing is decided here without consent — a version change clears the meters, never a console.
versioning.three_kinds: Three kinds of version move independently. Only the constitutional one touches the hardened surface — it alone passes the filter and the meters below; app releases and schema bumps move mechanically.
